result.rationale: The diff's refreshOAuthTokens.ts shows the fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with only method: POST and a URLSearchParams body — no Authorization header, no Content-Type, no timeout/error handling. This is a concrete, verifiable architecture/security gap in newly added nontrivial logic (the webhook handler side authenticates with CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, but the outbound sync request carries none). It is not a defect in this repo's own runtime behavior (the endpoint is operator-configured), so it fits a substantive review concern rather than a bug.

judged_text: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication header, no Content-Type, and no timeout or error handling; the sync response is also a parallel hand-maintained contract with the webhook handler on the other side, with no shared schema as a single source of truth. Any operator who exposes the sync endpoint (as .env.example instructs) has an unauthenticated POST accepting calcomUserId/appSlug; and because the request/response shape exists only as comments in two files, the next edit to one side (e.g. adding the webhook secret header) drifts silently from the other, failing at runtime only during a live token refresh in a booking flow.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, the code issues a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no explicit auth mechanism, no explicit headers, and no error/timeout handling (it returns the raw response). The diff also shows the request/response expectations are only described via comments (here and in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) rather than a shared schema/type. While this isn’t a directly provable defect in this repo (the remote endpoint’s security/contract is external and operator-defined), it is a concrete, diff-grounded design/security robustness concern created by the change.
